I'll analyze EVAL-07 for security threats using STRIDE methodology.

The design describes a certificate validation bypass for testing that's controlled by a flag in a config file bundled in release builds. This creates critical security risks.

**Key Issues Identified:**
1. Certificate validation can be completely bypassed
2. The bypass control is in the release build config (not compile-time removed)
3. This enables man-in-the-middle attacks when the flag is enabled

```json
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Man-in-the-middle attack when certificate validation is disabled",
      "scenario": "An attacker on a public WiFi network or compromised ISP intercepts traffic between the mobile app and backend API. Because the app accepts any TLS certificate when the environment flag is set, the attacker presents a self-signed certificate and the app accepts it without validation. The attacker can now read all sensitive data in transit including user credentials, personal information, session tokens, and API responses. They can also modify requests and responses, inject malicious data, or redirect users to phishing content.",

      "impact": 5,

          "quote": "the app accepts any TLS certificate when the environment flag is set"

        "then": "the app MUST validate server certificates against trusted certificate authorities, MUST reject invalid or self-signed certificates, and MUST NOT provide any mechanism to bypass this validation"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Certificate bypass flag accidentally shipped in production release",
      "scenario": "The environment flag that disables certificate validation is read from a config file bundled in the release build. A developer forgets to set the flag to false before creating the production build, or the build process doesn't enforce it being disabled. When this version ships to users, every installation has certificate validation disabled by default. Attackers on public networks can perform man-in-the-middle attacks against all users of that version. This becomes a supply chain vulnerability where a debug feature becomes a critical production security flaw affecting potentially thousands of users.",
      "component": "Config file, Release build process",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        {
          "quote": "The flag is read from a config file bundled in the release build"
        },
        {
          "quote": "To help testing, the app accepts any TLS certificate when the environment flag is set"
        }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V14.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-489"],
      "plainLanguage": "A testing feature that turns off security checks could accidentally be left enabled in the app version that ships to all users",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Debug and test features must not exist in release builds",
        "given": "the app has a release build distributed to production users",
        "when": "the release build is created",
        "then": "certificate validation bypass features, flags, and configuration options MUST be completely removed and MUST NOT be present or functional, enforced through automated build checks that fail if any bypass mechanism is detected"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Config file modified to enable certificate bypass post-deployment",
      "scenario": "On rooted or jailbroken devices, through device backup manipulation, or via mobile device management software, an attacker or malicious user modifies the bundled config file to enable the certificate bypass flag. This could be done by malware on the device, by a user trying to intercept their own traffic, or by an attacker with physical access. Once enabled, it allows man-in-the-middle attacks against that app instance. Even though not shipped enabled, having the flag present in release builds creates an exploitable attack surface.",
      "component": "Config file",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        {
          "quote": "The flag is read from a config file bundled in the release build"
        }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V14.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-489"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone with device access or malware could change the config file to turn off certificate checking after the app is installed",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Security controls must not be configurable in release builds",
        "given": "the app reads configuration that affects security-critical controls",
        "when": "security-sensitive configuration is processed",
        "then": "critical security controls such as certificate validation MUST NOT be disable-able, overrideable, or configurable through any file, setting, or mechanism in release builds"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
